Royal title in copies of papal letters associated with the 925/928 councils; late manuscript transmission; nineteenth-century coronation reconstruction and modern rejection of the Duvno location claim. Early reign dates and borders remain uncertain. Opening description and final text analysis: limestone screen slab, approximate date around 1100, Croatian Church Slavonic, transitional Glagolitic letters, Zvonimir's land grant and church building. Damaged readings remain debated. Archaeologia Adriatica 4 (2010), pp. 53-59, abstract: cemetery by St George above Kastel Sucurac, reidentification of the bronze fitting and late-eighth/early-ninth-century parallels. The object predates the tenth-century royal title evidence. American Journal of Physical Anthropology 148 (2012), pp. 543-556, DOI 10.1002/ajpa.22070; Table 1 and pp. 548-550: adult samples, early medieval millet interpretation and the distinct Sibenik-Sveti Lovre signal. Table A2 dates selected individuals; its dating ranges differ from the broad site labels, so no precise cemetery lifetime is adopted. Starohrvatska prosvjeta III/35 (2008), English abstract and full study pp. 211-238: ninth- to eleventh-century cemetery, skeletal and dental stress, small sample limitations and uncertain hunting interpretation. Skeletal similarity is not used to assign biological ethnicity. 1102 coronation at Biograd recorded in St Mary's Zadar cartulary; royal titles; Zadar's recognition in 1105 and the church inscription. This is dynastic change, not the disappearance of Croatian kingship or society.

Opening paragraph identifies Ocmulgee as an ancestral homeland of the Muscogee Nation. Earlier occupation of the place is not equated with the foundation of the later confederacy. Two-page site bulletin, Overview, Architecture and Interior: surviving clay floor, reconstructed upper building, seats, hearth and bird effigy. Dating is presented approximately rather than as an exact construction year; social-rank interpretation is questioned in the bulletin. Town organization, maternal clans, games, trade and 1840/1867 institutions. Outdated population, citizenship, McIntosh movement and 1975 constitution claims are not adopted; ratification is checked against the Nation's own constitutional record. The Council House: government rooms in use from 1878 to 1907, forced vacancy, later sale, return in 2010 and restoration in 2018. These dates refer to the building, not the Nation's existence.
